correctness.rationale: At each n-child node the m letter counts are independent Bin(n,1/2), giving an exact binomial sum for a unique plurality winner. A pair-tie local CLT gives u_m(n)=1/m-delta_m/sqrt(n)+o(n^-1/2) with delta_m>0; all triple ties are O(n^-1). The middle equality is possible exactly when n is in its prescribed residue class, and a triangular-array binomial local CLT gives probability (alpha_m+o(1))/sqrt(n), with alpha_m>0. Disjoint descendant-label sets yield independent root-child events, so at the root the false-negative probability is exp(-alpha_m sqrt(n)+o(sqrt(n)). A disjoint letter family implements each rational gate by a unique maximum and keeps independence. Thus every rational residue profile has the asserted limits. Direct finite tests cover 5276, 266508, 65536, 656 assignments at four layers of comparisons, and two numerical asymptotic parameter cases, with ALL_CHECKS_OK. Finite tests do not prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating paper poses convergence questions after demonstrating parity oscillation. This constructive theorem shows that all finite periodic patterns and all rational residue-limit profiles already arise with depth three in its unextended linear counting-modal language, explaining a substantial failure of a general convergence law. The exact binomial formulas and alpha_m exponent quantify the rare-event amplification mechanism and are reusable in probabilistic message-passing semantics. The claim is not a general decision procedure or minimum-depth theorem.
